messages:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 5xx and token latency on /v1/embeddings in eu-central-1. Auto-failover to secondary pool triggered. Pager muted.
Nora: saw the alert at 02:07 UTC. Metrics show tail latency jump ~2.3s and error rate to 6% for a 15m window. Failover executed at 02:12.
Sam: I joined the bridge, initial hypothesis: routing controller overloaded by a sudden fanout from a background job generating many long-context requests, caused request queue growth and worker OOMs in the primary pool.
Diego: taking the note on OOMs — kernel logs show multiple SIGKILLs from oom-killer on nodes gw-euc-03 and gw-euc-04. Memory fragmentation trace suggests slab exhaustion rather than KV eviction.
Amit: Customer-impact: two enterprise jobs (fintech-co-reporting, mobile-ai-sim) saw job timeouts and partial failures. Support ticket numbers INC-9921 and INC-9922 respectively. Both reported retries from their side which made the fanout worse.
Kelsey: from ops side, we temporarily isolated the offending job by blacklisting its client-id at the ingress for eu-central-1. That reduced inbound qps by ~40% and tail subsided. Blacklist command used:
```
rdw-ingress block-client --region eu-central-1 --client-id c-9f4a2 --reason "suspected runaway batch"
```
That unblocked the primary pool.
Nora: good quick mitigation. We need to schedule a postmortem and update runbooks for ingress runaway jobs + routing overload patterns. Proposed DRI: Sam for the postmortem doc.
Sam: I can be DRI. I'll draft RDW-POST-2350001234 and own the timeline and RCA. Planning a 45m postmortem tomorrow at 09:00 UTC.
Diego: I'll gather the node-level diagnostics and heap profiles, attach to the doc. Also opening RDW-OPS-9001 to repro the slab fragmentation locally and test kernel param changes.
Amit: I'll own customer comms. Draft to affected accounts: "We observed elevated latency and partial failures due to a runaway batch job triggering resource exhaustion; we applied mitigation and are conducting root cause analysis. We will follow up with timeline and mitigations." I'll wait to send until postmortem has timeline + remediation plan.
Kelsey: Runbook edits needed: add a new section `ingress-runaway` with steps to quickly identify and isolate heavy clients, and a short checklist to scale routing-controller and apply temporary client throttles. Also add note to verify fallback models' memory footprint before routing fallback.
Nora: action items — list owners + dates now:
- Sam: postmortem draft + timeline (48h) -> RDW-POST-2350001234
- Diego: node diag + repro ticket RDW-OPS-9001 (72h)
- Kelsey: runbook PR for `ingress-runaway` and throttle checklist (72h) -> RDW-RUN-9002
- Amit: customer communications + credit proposal (24h) -> INC-9921/2
- Nora: schedule postmortem + invite cross-team (24h)

Sam: note on routing fallback — the controller attempted to spill to a quantized variant but that variant wasn't registered for the embeddings model family in eu-central-1, which caused partial routing nail-ups. I'll add a gating check to ensure variant registration exists before fallback.
Diego: also found a race between ingress blacklist updates and controller config propagation; blacklist applied but controller still routed a few bursts for ~30s. We should make blacklist changes strongly consistent or use a dedicated token-bucket enforcement at the edge. Filed RDW-ENG-9003.
Kelsey: runbook snippet proposal:
```
1) verify `ingress.qps_per_client` via metrics
2) if a single client > 20% of traffic for 5m, run `rdw-ingress snapshot --client <id>`
3) apply temporary throttle: `rdw-ingress throttle --client <id> --qps 10 --expire 30m`
4) if controller fails to converge in 60s, escalate to routing oncall and consider full pool isolation
```
Add synthetic tests that simulate a 1% of traffic runaway every 6h to validate throttle flows.
Amit: for customer impact tracking — I'll tag each affected job with a status and attach retry logs. Also propose a small credit for impacted jobs; will propose amounts in 24h.
OpsBot: Reminder: create postmortem doc - `rdw create-postmortem --incident 2350001234 --owner Sam`
Nora: Sam — can you do the postmortem at 09:00 UTC tomorrow? If no, we have 10:30 as backup.
Sam: 09:00 works. I'll create the calendar invite and include oncall rotation, routing, infra, and support.
Diego: follow-up technical tasks I recommend: 1) kernel slab tuning experiment on canaries 2) add an alert for per-client 1m moving-window that spikes above threshold 3) ensure fallback variants are validated against model family registration table before traffic shift.
Kelsey: I'll open runbook PR branch `runbook/ingress-runaway-2350001234` and add the throttle automation snippets and the synthetic test harness.
Nora: final note — please link all tickets in the postmortem and record any SLO breaches. We'll do an exec summary for customer-facing comms after the postmortem. Thanks team. :pray:
incident-bot: Thread archived; postmortem scheduled.
